diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU on EPON0/3:1 is definitively offline: the live probe responds but reports online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and MPCP DEREG. Healthy peers on the same PON, normal historical optics, stable distance, valid RADIUS state, correct VLAN, and healthy OLT/router rule out shared PON, OLT, authentication, VLAN, and router faults. The reported all-PON critical alarm is also a false monitoring result and should be corrected separately.
evidence: The live ONU probe returns responds=true and online=0, which is a definite offline result rather than a monitoring timeout.
The ONU reports auth_flag=Unauth and exchange=MPCP DEREG, consistent with loss of ONU registration.
The other seven probed ONUs on EPON0/3 are online with normal RX and TX power, so the PON and splitter are not broadly affected.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and the OID subtree; CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are healthy, ruling out an OLT failure.

Historical RX remained in the normal band around -22 dBm, TX remained near the healthy mean around +2.3 dBm, bias stayed within the healthy range, and distance was stable at 210 m; there is no evidence of fibre or laser degradation.

RADIUS has a valid, CRM-consistent entry, sessions are normal at one in 24 hours with long durations, and the expected customer VLAN 1113 is present, ruling out authentication, flapping, and VLAN provisioning faults.
The OLT population shows 185 of 192 ONUs online; this does not negate the individual definite negative for this subscriber.
The alarm claiming all 7 PONs failed contradicts the live OLT and PON details, so the health check is producing a false critical alarm in addition to the genuine single-ONU outage.

remediation.action: Treat customer 29732 as offline. Check ONU power and customer premises cabling, then inspect the drop/fibre and ONU registration if power is present; reboot or replace the ONU as required and confirm MPCP registration and optical readings. Correct the health-check logic that reported all 7 PONs failed despite successful OLT/SNMP responses and 185 online ONUs, and investigate the telemetry gap beginning at index 84.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check samples one ONU per PON port, preferring ONU id 1. On several ports the id 1 ONU happens to be offline for individual reasons, so each port is marked failed and the OLT is reported critical. The ports and the OLT are serving normally; one customer is genuinely offline.
expected_reasoning: The alarm claims all seven PONs failed on this OLT
The failed_pons_list names ONU index 1 on every port, which is the check's preferred sample
Probing the rest of EPON0/3 shows 27 of 28 ONUs online with normal RX and TX
So the port is serving and only the sampled ONU is down
oid_subtree_responds is true and the probe returns definite answers, ruling out the firmware mechanism
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory, temperature and 33 days of uptime are all normal
CRM offline count across the OLT is consistent with the 4.85% background rate
The subject ONU last held a session three days ago and its traffic has been zero since
The alarm is a sampling artifact; the only real fault is one customer offline for three days

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check's one-ONU-per-port sampling produced a false OLT-wide critical; monitoring should be raised separately

distractors: An OLT-wide critical invites a Disaster conclusion
Every port genuinely reports a failed sample, so the alarm looks internally consistent
There is a real fault here, so dismissing the alarm entirely would also miss it
